# Samebase

> Samebase standardizes web apps on the best stack we have found: code in the user's GitHub
> repository, a Convex backend, and Cloudflare Workers delivery. Once you have found the best
> stack, repeat it. Each new app adds a product, not another system to maintain.

Samebase can create a new app in about a minute or connect an existing GitHub repository without
touching its providers. A connected app can remain GitHub-only or attach Convex and Cloudflare
later. One repository can contain several explicit app roots for a monorepo; humans configure those
roots in the dashboard.

The dashboard gives humans one inventory of every app they connect, its app roots, provider
resources, current state, direct provider coordinates, and provider or connection repair actions.
Samebase does not replace the coding-agent interface the user already chose: Codex, Claude Code,
Cursor, or any MCP client can call its actions over MCP.

Apps created through Samebase live in the user's own GitHub, Convex, and Cloudflare accounts.
Deleting the Samebase account does not stop a running app. The knowledge is free: anyone can build
the identical stack with no Samebase account.

The `.md` links under Docs return raw markdown, and the same paths without `.md` serve the
HTML pages. Action and operate docs are raw markdown only.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://samebase.com/landing-preview): why the base is GitHub, Convex, and Cloudflare,
  how it scales across connected apps, and the leaving test
- [The stack](https://samebase.com/docs/the-stack.md): what the app template ships and why each
  piece was chosen
- [Do it yourself](https://samebase.com/docs/do-it-yourself.md): deploy the same stack by hand, for
  $0/month, with no Samebase account
- [Receipts](https://samebase.com/docs/receipts.md): every factual claim with its primary source
  and the date it was last checked
- [Pricing](https://samebase.com/pricing.md): what stays free, what will be metered, and why there
  is no price list yet

## Actions

Every operational action has one contract, and these are the same actions the dashboard buttons run.
Degraded app states name their remedy in a `nextAction` field whose values are these action ids.

- [Get authentication status](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/get_authentication_status.md): Read the caller's current Samebase MCP authentication state: account identity, role, access keys, and OAuth token scopes.
- [Get user vaults](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/get_user_vaults.md): List the Samebase apps and repositories available to the authenticated user, including provisioning state and provider resources. Degraded states carry a nextAction field naming the repair action that fixes them.
- [Create repository](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/create_repository.md): Create a new Samebase app by starting the managed app provisioning workflow: create the GitHub repository, seed the starter app, provision Convex, and provision Cloudflare.
- [Connect existing repository](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/connect_existing_repository.md): Import an existing GitHub repository as a Samebase app. Creates the Samebase record and syncs the repository tree; Convex and Cloudflare stay unconfigured until explicitly attached.
- [List convex projects](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/list_convex_projects.md): List the Convex projects available on the caller's connected Convex account, for choosing an attach target.
- [List cloudflare accounts](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/list_cloudflare_accounts.md): List the Cloudflare accounts available on the caller's connected Cloudflare login, for choosing where a Worker lives.
- [List cloudflare workers](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/list_cloudflare_workers.md): List the Workers on a Cloudflare account, classified against the app's repository so safe attach targets are marked recommended.
- [Connect convex deployment](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/connect_convex_deployment.md): Attach an existing Convex project to a Samebase app (manual attach): records the deployment and starts the connection run.
- [Connect cloudflare worker](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/connect_cloudflare_worker.md): Attach an existing Cloudflare Worker to a Samebase app (manual attach): validates the Worker against the repository and starts the connection run.
- [Wire builds](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/wire_builds.md): Connect the app's Cloudflare Worker to its GitHub repository through Workers Builds: production and preview triggers, so pushes deploy and pull requests get previews.
- [Wire convex build access](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/wire_convex_build_access.md): Mint Convex deploy keys for the app and place both CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY and PREVIEW_CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY into its Workers Builds triggers.
- [Verify infrastructure](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/verify_infrastructure.md): Verify the app's recorded Cloudflare infrastructure: Workers Builds trigger IDs and Convex deploy-key variables, then mark stale Samebase records as repairable.
- [Retry infrastructure provisioning](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/retry_infrastructure_provisioning.md): Retry a failed managed provisioning run for a Samebase-managed app, resuming from the failed step.
- [Create browser handoff](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/create_browser_handoff.md): Create a short-lived one-time Samebase browser sign-in URL for the MCP grant's current user. The URL is sensitive and expires quickly.

## Operate

- [MCP server](https://api.samebase.com/mcp): connect a coding agent over MCP (OAuth happens in the
  browser); the tools are the actions listed above.
- [Production logs](https://samebase.com/docs/operate/production-logs.md): read backend and Worker
  logs provider-direct, with coordinates from get_user_vaults
- [Custom domain](https://samebase.com/docs/operate/custom-domain.md): attach a domain to the
  app's Worker in your own Cloudflare account
